Yes. It's a real app, and it's running.

One Bun process on your Mac serves the web UI to you and the tools to the agents. It is up now at http://localhost:7420 with five machines and five real runs in it, the ones from tonight's evals.

Where
localhost:7420
One process: bun src/cli.ts serve in ~/oss/machine. Started tonight; it stays up until you stop it.
Data
~/.machine/machine.db
One SQLite file. Every machine, every run, every step an agent reported. Nothing leaves the machine.
Agents reach it by
/mcp
Claude Code connects once: claude mcp add --transport http machine http://localhost:7420/mcp. Published skills land in ~/.claude/skills/.

How the pieces fit

The agent never holds the state. It asks for the next step, does it, reports, and the server says what is allowed next. A wrong event is rejected and shows up in the UI as a rejected call. You see every move as it happens.

The screens, live from port 7420 tonight

Runs. Every run, with what needs you on top. One is blocked, waiting on a decision.

A blocked run. The agent could not finish honestly, so it stopped and wrote what you must decide. The checklist and "I fixed it, resume" are the whole hand-off.

A finished run. History on the left is the agent's own record, step by step. The graph on the right is the machine with the path it took.

The editor. States, events, what to report, written as an outline; the graph and the SKILL.md update as you type. Publish writes the skill to ~/.claude/skills.

The stack, and why

PartChoiceWhy
Runtime + serverBun 1.3, HonoOne binary, one process, SQLite built in. Nothing to install for a local tool.
Agent connectionMCP, Streamable HTTP, @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3The standard way Claude Code and other agents call tools. Six tools: list, preflight, begin, transition, note, fail, get.
State engineour own, ~30 linesValidate the event, the actor, and the output payload against the definition; append to history. XState was weighed and not needed yet.
Storagebun:sqlite, WAL, one fileRuns are an append-only history. A file in your home is enough and easy to back up.
Live UIServer-Sent EventsOne open connection, the UI redraws on every change. No polling, no websocket plumbing.
UIReact 19, Vite 8, Tailwind 4, dagre, GeistFamiliar dashboard shell; the graph is hand-drawn SVG laid out by dagre.
Proofclaude -p evals, Playwright, an LLM judgeNo unit tests. Each eval is a fresh Claude Code session running a published skill in a throwaway repo; we check the run's own history in SQLite and the files it produced.
Guardrailsnone yetDecided from data: 20 runs across four machines, zero rejected calls, so nothing has been added.

Size: about 1,400 lines of TypeScript and CSS across engine, server, CLI and UI; ten runtime dependencies. Full reasoning and sources in DECISIONS.md.

What has been proven

changelog-draft55 ready05 pass

Dry runs use stand-in repos with a stub gh and npm so nothing touches GitHub. The ship-fix machine exists and was driven from the UI, but no agent has run it for real because a real run opens a PR.

Try it in three commands

open http://localhost:7420                                   # it is already running
claude mcp add --transport http machine http://localhost:7420/mcp   # once, so Claude Code can call it
# then, in any Claude Code session:  "run the changelog-draft skill on this repo, version 0.2.0"

Stop it with pkill -f "src/cli.ts serve". Dev loop for the UI: bunx vite alongside the server.
